Section B
Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
Looking for a job after 45
研究说明：数据来自 Generation 于 2021 年 3–5 月在七国开展的调查，45+主要指 45–60 岁入门或中级岗位人群；63%是当时已失业超过一年者的比例，不是未来概率。培训信心 75%与工资补贴 41%，不是三倍实际录用率；态度相关性不证明因果，低收入群体也面临费用和时间障碍。
A) Ageism and long-term unemployment can be especially damaging for those in the second half of their careers. Changing careers is hard. Getting back into work after you’ve been laid off is even harder. Older workers have made up a large share of the long-term unemployed in several countries. Some hiring managers admit they are reluctant to hire those over 40 or 45, arguing they probably won’t be a good “fit,” their experience won’t be relevant to the workplace, and they’ll be unable or unwilling to learn new skills.
B) What may improve prospects? More education and training. These are findings from a 2021 survey by Generation, a nonprofit founded by former McKinsey consultants. The study collected 3,800 responses from workers and job seekers and 1,404 from hiring managers in seven countries between March and May 2021. Its main older group was aged 45–60 and seeking or working in entry-level or intermediate roles.
C) The report cited national statistics showing that older age groups accounted for substantial shares of long-term unemployment, though age bands and duration thresholds differed by country. In its own survey, 63 percent of unemployed respondents aged 45–60 had already been jobless for over a year, versus 36 percent of those aged 18–34. This describes respondents at the time of the survey; it is not a prediction of any newly unemployed person’s chances. The authors viewed age-related barriers as a serious concern.
D) A substantial part of this, they report, is “widespread ageism” on the part of hiring managers. Although such managers admit that post-45 hires turn out on average to be just as good as or better than younger workers, they still don’t want to hire them. “Hiring managers have a strong perception bias against 45+ job candidates — they believe that members of this age group have poor skills and low adaptability,” Generation’s analysts report.
E) The survey results are remarkable. Hiring managers are three times as likely to rate job applicants age 35–44 as a better “fit” than those over 45. They rate the post-45 job seekers lower on average on all three measures — even experience — than those ages 18 to 34. This is true even though the managers’ responses rated 87 percent of their hires aged 45+ as performing as well as or better than younger peers.
F) Their biggest fears about hiring those over 45? Managers said they worry that older hires will be reluctant to try new technologies, and will be unable to learn new skills. Most surveyed hiring managers were under 45. The report suggested that similarity in age might contribute to their preferences, rather than establishing a causal explanation.
G) But here's the good news. Relevant education and training may improve perceptions of older applicants. Three-quarters of hiring managers selected a reputable, profession-specific training program as something that would increase their hiring confidence; 73 percent selected a recognized industry certification (文凭). Among those over 45 who’d successfully switched careers, 74% said training helped them get their new job.
H) “Midcareer switchers overwhelmingly say that training enabled them to shift to a new career path,” the analysts write. When they asked over-45 candidates about their attitudes, they found an association, not proof of causation: “those who are excited by training are unemployed for less time, receive more job offers, and are more satisfied by the job offers they receive.”
I) Reputable training was selected as a confidence booster by 75 percent of hiring managers, compared with 41 percent for government wage subsidies (补贴). These figures measure stated preferences, not actual hiring rates. What training are we talking about? Obviously it depends on the job. And, yes, managers are most likely to be impressed by industry qualifications you get in school. These things cost money, and time. But these aren’t the only things helpful. Those who had successfully changed careers after 45 told Generation that education and training had been a big help — and that included in-person, on-the-job training, “informal learning,” and online courses — with or without certification.
J) If they think we’re too old to learn new skills after we’re 45, just learning some new skills may have an effect on its own. There’s a downside to this. Among survey respondents aged 45+ who were not keen on training, many had limited incomes or a secondary education or less. The report suggested that cost, time and negative past experiences with education could be barriers. In the survey, midcareer job switchers with higher incomes participated in 2.5 training programs each. Those with lower incomes: 0.9 programs on average.
K) Relevant work experience may also help employers see how a candidate could contribute. As an illustration, a literature graduate who has worked in a bank might be more prepared for a particular banking role than a finance graduate with no practical experience. This is a possible example, not a universal rule: the role, qualifications and individual abilities matter.
L) Addressing ageism requires employers and society to act, while relevant training can also help job seekers. And it’s easy to forget that employers, like everyone else, are under time pressure and are just trying to solve problems. Relevant, credible training, including some inexpensive and informal learning, may help address employers’ concerns. The internet provides additional ways to learn new skills, including free educational videos and paid courses. Availability, quality and suitability vary.
M) Bottom line? Yes, it really can be difficult getting a new job after age 45, let alone changing careers. One of the best things we can do to help ourselves is to go online and learn new, relevant skills. The report also highlights barriers facing people with fewer resources, raising a challenge for society as a whole. Not only do we not want to see lives go to waste, but we all benefit if more people are working and fewer are unemployed.

Passage One
Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
阅读说明：本篇回顾 2021 年改菜单、2022 年获评事件；首获三星对应 2012 版指南。餐厅后来再次提供部分动物性菜品，不能把历史纯素菜单当作现状。三星评价烹饪而非授予个人，也不是健康或全行业增长认证。
In 2022, New York's Eleven Madison Park became the first restaurant to retain three Michelin stars with an entirely plant-based, or vegan (纯素的), tasting menu.
The fine dining establishment received its first three-star rating in the 2012 Michelin Guide when the menu was famed for its fancy animal-based dishes.
In 2021, the restaurant’s chef and owner, Daniel Humm, made the bold decision to remove meat from the menu, citing our unsustainable food system. The change applied to its tasting menu; the original report noted that dairy milk remained available for tea and coffee.
At the time, Humm acknowledged the move was risky, admitting that “it wasn’t clear if guests would come”, but called the gamble “a risk worth taking.”
“In view of the climate crisis, I didn’t want to open the same restaurant,” Humm told the Financial Times in an interview. “If we can show the possibilities of eating plant-based food in this setting, it can open a lot of doors” for others to follow.
The 2022 award supported Eleven Madison Park’s decision to take meat off the menu and embrace plant-based foods, with Michelin’s 2022 New York guide branding it a “bold vision of luxury dining”.
“We took the jump to transform Eleven Madison Park into a plant-based fine dining restaurant knowing in our hearts this is what we believed in,” stated Humm on Instagram. “Last night, we were honored to be awarded three Michelin stars for the 11th year in a row. I am so grateful to the team members who contributed through its nearly 25-year history. We are also grateful to our guests and partners who believed in our vision and encouraged us to push harder.”
Three stars are Michelin’s highest culinary (烹饪的) distinction, awarded to restaurants for their cooking. This recognition showed that a plant-based menu could meet that standard. It did not certify every vegan dish as healthier or measure an industry-wide trend.
“I think luxury companies have a real role to play and a responsibility,” says Humm. “The more creative we are, the more beautiful and delicious our future will be.”

A) It became the first to retain three Michelin stars with an entirely plant-based tasting menu.
B) It is the first restaurant in the city to remove meat from its menu.
C) It was famed throughout the U.S. for its fancy regional dishes.
D) It was established as a three-star Michelin restaurant in 2011.
47. What environmental reason did Daniel Humm give when he decided to remove meat from the menu of his restaurant?
A) To encourage more customers to be vegan.
B) To contribute to a sustainable food system.
C) To show the appeal of a plant-based menu.
D) To strive for the three-star Michelin rating.
48. How did Humm assess the risk before knowing whether guests would come?
A) It was a worthwhile effort even though he was unsure of its success.
B) It would set a model for many more restaurants to follow.
C) It was a mad gamble few chefs in the fine dining world would risk taking.
D) It would prove a right step to take in today’s catering business.
49. What does the phrase “bold vision of luxury dining” convey about the restaurant’s 2022 approach?
A) It elevates the restaurant’s cooking to an art form.
B) It proves the validity of ratings awarded by Michelin.
C) It shows a daring foresight regarding future fine dining.
D) It is an effort to transform the restaurant into a luxury one.
50. What does the awarding of three Michelin stars to Eleven Madison Park indicate?
A) An optimistic vision of vegan foods becoming mainstream.
B) A greater responsibility for the culinary world to undertake.
C) A strong incentive for more restaurants to offer healthier foods to their customers.
D) Recognition that a plant-based menu can meet Michelin’s highest cooking standard.
Passage Two
Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
研究说明：遗传检测的变异识别、疾病风险预测与个人诊断是不同问题；单基因检测也有适用范围和解释限制，祖源百分比是参考数据库估计。复杂性状存在遗传关联，不能据此保证测出个人天赋或理想伴侣。第 52、53、55 题同步修正，55 题移除原 C/D 语义重叠。
With genetic testing becoming increasingly popular, many people are left wondering exactly how accurate it is. Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want information about inherited health risks, including some inborn (先天的) conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon.
How accurate DNA tests are relies greatly upon the kind of test being taken, on the specific question you ask, and on how complex the genetics behind a trait (特征) is. For example, a validated test for a well-understood single-gene disorder can identify a relevant DNA variant more directly than a test trying to predict a complex trait. Finding a variant does not always determine whether or when symptoms will occur.
Ancestry tests claim to reveal our genetic identities. Their geographical percentages are estimates based on comparisons with reference populations. They do not specify nationality or give a complete family history, and estimates can differ across databases and methods.
What about using DNA tests to discover distant family members? There are tools to compare one’s DNA with others’ to find distant relatives based on their genetic identification. Evidence for close biological relationships is usually clearer than for distant ones. The reliability of a match depends on the test, the shared DNA and the comparison database.
Genetic health tests claim to be able to detect certain hereditary (遗传的) diseases, or other health conditions. Clinical tests can help confirm some genetic conditions. Many common diseases, however, cannot be diagnosed or predicted by DNA results alone; interpretation also depends on clinical and family information.
Many of our traits and common diseases also depend upon non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others.
Genetic tests for multifactorial traits are often very tricky to interpret. Height, for example, is influenced by many genetic variants as well as environmental factors; some rare variants can have large effects. A test can look at many genes at once, but it’s difficult to predict how they will play together. Then you should also account for non-genetic factors that are not written in the DNA.
Claims that a DNA test alone can identify a perfect romantic partner or reliably determine a person’s personality or talents should not be accepted as established science. Genetic associations with traits do exist, but these do not justify such deterministic promises about an individual.
51. What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests?
A) Knowing their accuracy.
B) Evaluating their applicability.
C) Utilizing the information they provide.
D) Weighing the consequences they have.
52. What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable?
A) Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait.
B) Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases.
C) Those focusing on the specific questions being asked.
D) Validated tests for well-understood single-gene disorders.
53. What limitation does the passage identify for DNA testing of many common diseases?
A) They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves.
B) They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors.
C) DNA results alone cannot diagnose or predict many common diseases.
D) They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment.
54. What difficulty does the passage identify in predicting the combined effects of many genes?
A) The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene.
B) The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact.
C) The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones.
D) The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved.
55. What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents?
A) They are solid scientific bases for application.
B) They are helpful in finding a romantic match.
C) They require only one gene to predict complex talents.
D) Their promise to determine such traits from DNA alone is not established science.
